electionType: Wayne Township Municipal (5th Ward) & Board of Education General Election
councilStructure: Wayne Township Council (Mayor-Council Plan F under Faulkner Act). 9 Council Members (6 Ward, 3 At-Large). In 2026, voters in the 5th Ward elect a Council representative for an unexpired term, alongside township-wide School Board trustees.
certifiedTaxRateContext: 2.748% Total Certified Tax Rate (2026). Equalization Ratio 80.4%.
unanimousHealthBenefitPledge: Township Council and BOE candidates maintain strict ethics standards regarding municipal healthcare benefit waivers and pension transparency.

votingResources.electionDayHours: 6:00 AM – 8:00 PM EST on Tuesday, November 3, 2026

councilCandidates.name: Matthew Cavallo
councilCandidates.experience: Appointed/Elected Wayne 5th Ward Councilman; seasoned credentialed New Jersey Municipal Administrator (QPA/CMFO) with decades of local government budgeting expertise.
councilCandidates.tagline: Professional municipal fiscal management, rigorous capital budgeting, and aggressive Pompton River flood basin mitigation.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Willowbrook Ratable Shield & Debt Control
keyPlatformPillars.details: Safeguard Wayne commercial tax base following Toys R Us loss and mall appeals; optimize municipal debt portfolio to protect single-family homeowners.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Passaic & Pompton River Flood Action
keyPlatformPillars.details: Capture federal FEMA and NJDEP flood resilience grants for desilting, culvert reinforcement, and repetitive-loss property elevation.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Zero-Based Municipal Budget Reviews
keyPlatformPillars.details: Apply professional municipal manager standards to Wayne $83.5M operating budget; require department heads to justify all discretionary expenditures.

quotes: Wayne homeowners deserve professional municipal expertise. We must manage every dollar with zero-based discipline, protect our ratable base, and defend our neighborhoods from devastating floods.
councilCandidates.civicBackground: Lifelong Passaic County public administrator, Wayne 5th Ward civic organizer, and municipal finance specialist.

investigativeDossier.disclosuresAndFDS: Discloses municipal management credentials; standard Local Government Ethics Law filing.
investigativeDossier.cleanRecordVerification: Verified Clean Public Record — No court judgments, municipal censures, or ethics violations on public record.
investigativeDossier.conflictOfInterestWatch: Must recuse from any municipal contracts involving current or past consulting clients.

historicExperience.summary: Over 15 years in municipal governance and public administration across northern New Jersey.

careerTimeline.details: Represents 5th Ward neighborhoods focusing on infrastructure and municipal services.
Directs municipal procurement, capital bonding, and municipal budgeting.

educationAndCredentials: Certified New Jersey Municipal Finance Officer (CMFO)
civicLeadership: Pompton River flood mitigation taskforce advocate

interviewStances.interviewSource: Passaic County Clerk Candidate Statements & TAPinto Wayne Candidate Forum
interviewStances.taxesAndSpending: Disciplined capital spending and restructuring debt to hold Wayne municipal tax increases well below state caps.
interviewStances.zoningAndDataCenters: Opposes industrial mega-warehouses and high-density variances; supports smart redevelopment of vacant corporate parks along Route 23.
interviewStances.floodingAndWater: Aggressive partnership with Army Corps of Engineers and NJDEP for Pompton River basin dredging and localized stormwater upgrades.
interviewStances.governanceAndDecorum: Brings collaborative municipal management discipline to council workshops and open public dialogue.
interviewStances.publicSafetyAndTraffic: Fully funds Wayne Police Department patrol staffing, radar enforcement on Valley Road and Hamburg Turnpike, and school safety officers.
interviewStances.cannabisLicensing: Supports current zoning buffer restrictions keeping commercial cannabis away from school zones.
interviewStances.keyInterviewQuote: We must bring modern, professional fiscal management to Wayne Town Hall to protect homeowners from commercial ratable erosion.

councilCandidates.name: Dennis Marnick
councilCandidates.experience: Longtime Wayne resident and 5th Ward community leader with senior corporate executive background in operational efficiency and contract negotiation.
councilCandidates.tagline: Independent citizen watchdog oversight, neighborhood traffic safety, and total transparency in township vendor contracts.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Forensic Vendor Contract Audit
keyPlatformPillars.details: Commission independent reviews of all recurring legal, engineering, and architectural vendor agreements to cut township overhead.

keyPlatformPillars.title: 5th Ward Traffic Calming & Pedestrian Safety
keyPlatformPillars.details: Install speed feedback signs and pedestrian crosswalk beacons along cut-through routes connecting Valley Road and French Hill.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Evening Public Workshops & Live Q&A
keyPlatformPillars.details: Expand public comment opportunities at Town Hall and broadcast all council committee meetings with live online streaming.

quotes: Wayne residents need an independent watchdog on the council who will scrutinize every vendor invoice and fight for 5th Ward neighborhoods.
councilCandidates.civicBackground: Wayne resident for over 25 years; active youth sports booster and civic association volunteer.

investigativeDossier.disclosuresAndFDS: Discloses corporate private sector leadership; clean financial record.
investigativeDossier.cleanRecordVerification: Verified Clean Public Record — No legal judgments, ethics citations, or financial irregularities on file.
investigativeDossier.conflictOfInterestWatch: Standard corporate ethics firewalls for commercial vendors.

verifiedSources.title: Passaic County Clerk Official Candidate Filing

historicExperience.summary: Over 20 years managing enterprise budgets, supply chain contracts, and corporate teams.

careerTimeline.details: Directs commercial contracts, vendor procurement, and operating budgets.

educationAndCredentials: Bachelor of Science in Business Management

interviewStances.interviewSource: Passaic County Candidate Filings & Local Civic Debates
interviewStances.taxesAndSpending: Demands forensic spending reviews, zero-based budgeting, and ending automatic contract renewals for outside professionals.
interviewStances.zoningAndDataCenters: Strict opposition to overdevelopment, warehouse rezoning, or commercial encroachment into quiet suburban residential streets.
interviewStances.floodingAndWater: Demands immediate localized stormwater conduit clearing and rapid deployment of flood protection resources during storm events.
interviewStances.governanceAndDecorum: Independent council voice holding township leadership accountable for project timelines and costs.
interviewStances.publicSafetyAndTraffic: Increased traffic enforcement on residential cut-through streets and enhanced safety zones around neighborhood schools.
interviewStances.cannabisLicensing: Opposed to retail cannabis outlets in residential and highway corridors.
interviewStances.keyInterviewQuote: Taxpayers are tired of rubber-stamped budgets. We need fresh leadership and relentless accountability on the Wayne Council.

boeCandidates.name: Joseph "Joe" Troy Jr.
boeCandidates.term: Full 3-Year Term (2027–2029) • Vote for up to 3 (6 Running)
boeCandidates.experience: Wayne parent, active school volunteer, and financial operations professional with 18+ years corporate budgeting experience.
boeCandidates.keyFocus: Expanding STEM and vocational pathways, fiscal transparency in the $186.2M school budget, and classroom technology upgrades.
boeCandidates.fiscalStance: Promotes line-item budget transparency and competitive professional contract bidding to keep Wayne school taxes affordable.
boeCandidates.infrastructureStance: Prioritizes proactive roof and HVAC climate control maintenance across Wayne 14 school buildings.

interviewStances.interviewSource: Passaic County Clerk Certified Filing & Wayne BOE Candidates Forum
interviewStances.keyPriorities: Educational excellence, transparent school spending, and empowering parents and educators.
interviewStances.facilitiesAndBudget: Focuses on long-range capital planning to avoid emergency tax referendums.
interviewStances.keyInterviewQuote: We must provide our children with world-class education while respecting the taxpayers who fund our public schools.

boeCandidates.name: Burcin Ogrenir
boeCandidates.term: Full 3-Year Term (2027–2029) • Vote for up to 3 (6 Running)
boeCandidates.experience: Educational researcher, university professor, and mother of Wayne Public Schools students with extensive background in curriculum development and early childhood education.
boeCandidates.keyFocus: Closing academic achievement gaps, supporting special education programs, and strengthening teacher retention.
boeCandidates.fiscalStance: Advocates directing the maximum possible percentage of the $186.2M budget directly into classroom instruction and special needs support.
boeCandidates.infrastructureStance: Supports school safety vestibules, modern classroom learning environments, and ADA accessibility.

interviewStances.interviewSource: Wayne BOE Candidate Forums & Official Campaign Platform
interviewStances.keyPriorities: Inclusive education, evidence-based academic curricula, and mental health support for students.
interviewStances.facilitiesAndBudget: Prioritizes classroom resources over administrative expansion.
interviewStances.keyInterviewQuote: Every child in Wayne deserves an individualized pathway to academic and personal success.

boeCandidates.name: Donald Pavlak
boeCandidates.term: Full 3-Year Term (2027–2029) • Vote for up to 3 (6 Running)
boeCandidates.experience: Long-serving veteran Trustee and former President of the Wayne Board of Education; lifelong Wayne resident with decades of board governance experience.
boeCandidates.keyFocus: Board continuity, labor contract stability, defending state education aid, and expanding Advanced Placement (AP) curricula.
boeCandidates.fiscalStance: Maintains a record of balanced budgets within state 2% caps while preserving comprehensive athletic and music programs.
boeCandidates.infrastructureStance: Led major energy efficiency, solar installation, and security vestibule upgrades across Wayne Valley and Wayne Hills High Schools.

interviewStances.interviewSource: Wayne Board of Education Records & Candidate Statements
interviewStances.keyPriorities: Experienced, steady governance, protecting school funding, and supporting frontline teachers.
interviewStances.facilitiesAndBudget: Prudent multi-year capital reserve planning to modernize aging school facilities without spikes in tax levy.
interviewStances.keyInterviewQuote: Experience matters when governing a $186M district. We have maintained top academic ratings while protecting taxpayers.

boeCandidates.name: Wendy Limandri
boeCandidates.term: Full 3-Year Term (2027–2029) • Vote for up to 3 (6 Running)
boeCandidates.experience: Wayne parent, active PTO officer, and community advocate running on the 'Trusted, Transparent, Together' slate with Pavlak and Faber.
boeCandidates.keyFocus: Parent-teacher communication, student wellness, modernizing elementary reading programs, and school facility cleanliness.
boeCandidates.fiscalStance: Advocates shared purchasing agreements with the township to lower transportation and insurance costs.
boeCandidates.infrastructureStance: Supports playground safety modernizations, school air filtration, and secure perimeter access controls.

interviewStances.keyPriorities: Parental involvement, educational rigor, and cooperative community governance.
interviewStances.facilitiesAndBudget: Focuses on transparent budget presentations so parents understand where educational tax dollars go.
interviewStances.keyInterviewQuote: Strong schools build strong communities. Working together transparently, we can elevate Wayne schools to new heights.

boeCandidates.name: Mark Faber
boeCandidates.term: Full 3-Year Term (2027–2029) • Vote for up to 3 (6 Running)
boeCandidates.experience: Incumbent Wayne Board of Education Trustee; healthcare finance professional with deep experience in enterprise budgeting and benefits management.
boeCandidates.keyFocus: District healthcare cost containment, healthcare benefit pooling, special education funding, and academic excellence.
boeCandidates.fiscalStance: Applies corporate financial analysis to health benefit reserves and out-of-district tuition contracts to eliminate waste.
boeCandidates.infrastructureStance: Advocates preventive maintenance schedules for heating, ventilation, and athletic facilities.

interviewStances.interviewSource: Wayne BOE Public Meeting Records & Candidate Interviews
interviewStances.keyPriorities: Healthcare benefit cost control, supporting district staff, and maintaining fiscal discipline.
interviewStances.facilitiesAndBudget: Leverages financial expertise to ensure Wayne gets maximum value from every taxpayer dollar.
interviewStances.keyInterviewQuote: As a finance professional, I scrutinize our district spending to ensure our resources go where they belong: into the classroom.

boeCandidates.name: James Fera
boeCandidates.term: Full 3-Year Term (2027–2029) • Vote for up to 3 (6 Running)
boeCandidates.experience: Wayne parent, educator, and grassroots advocate focused on nonpartisan school governance, student mental health, and academic fundamentals.
boeCandidates.keyFocus: Keeping national political polarization out of Wayne classrooms, boosting math and reading proficiency, and expanding extracurriculars.
boeCandidates.fiscalStance: Calls for an independent line-by-line audit of district administrative spending and consultant contracts.
boeCandidates.infrastructureStance: Supports upgrading school science labs, technology infrastructure, and athletic facilities.

interviewStances.interviewSource: Passaic County Clerk Candidate Filing & Local Community Forum
interviewStances.keyPriorities: Putting student academic outcomes first, rejecting partisan culture wars, and fiscal accountability.
interviewStances.facilitiesAndBudget: Demands strict accountability for outside legal and consulting expenditures.
interviewStances.keyInterviewQuote: Our public schools should be about students, teachers, and learning—not political agendas.

ballotArchitecture.summary: Wayne voters cast ballots for local representation (5th Ward Council & Board of Education), County government (Passaic County Commissioners & Surrogate), and Federal offices (U.S. Senate & U.S. House NJ-11).

offices.description: Governs the $83.5M municipal operating budget, Wayne Police Department, DPW, parks, and local ordinances for Wayne Township.
Oversees 14 public schools, ~7,500 students, and the $186.2M Wayne Township Public Schools operating budget.
Allocates the ~$500M Passaic County budget, maintaining county roadways in Wayne (Valley Rd, French Hill Rd, Hamburg Turnpike), Passaic County Community College, and county parks.
Constitutional Officer managing wills, estates, guardianships, and adoption records across Passaic County.

offices.office: United States Senate (New Jersey, Class II)
offices.taxShare: Federal SALT Deduction Relief & Infrastructure Grants
offices.description: Represents New Jersey in the U.S. Senate. Justin Murphy (R), Cory Booker (D), Veronica Fernandez (End The Corruption!), and Joanne Kuniansky (Socialist Workers Party).

offices.taxShare: Federal Flood Control & Community Project Earmarks
offices.description: Represents Wayne, Parsippany, Montclair, Morristown, and Montville in Congress. Analilia Mejia (D) vs. Joe Hathaway (R), Alan Bond, and Vincent Matrisciano.

usSenate.office: United States Senate (New Jersey, Class II)
usSenate.importance: Represents New Jersey in Washington D.C., confirming federal judges, voting on federal budgets, and fighting for SALT deduction relief for high-tax suburban homeowners.

candidates.name: Justin Murphy
candidates.keyPriorities: Federal spending restraint, full SALT deduction restoration, national border security, and energy independence.
candidates.localImpact: Pledges to cut federal red tape delaying Passaic River Basin flood mitigation projects.

candidates.name: Cory Booker
candidates.role: U.S. Senator (in office since 2013); former Mayor of Newark.
candidates.keyPriorities: Repealing the federal $10K SALT deduction cap, funding NJ Transit and Gateway Tunnel, and clean water infrastructure grants.
candidates.localImpact: Secured federal appropriations for regional flood defense and water treatment infrastructure in Passaic County.

candidates.name: Veronica Fernandez
candidates.role: Civic activist running on anti-corruption platform.
candidates.keyPriorities: Term limits, campaign finance reform, and reducing cost-of-living burdens on middle-class families.

candidates.name: Joanne Kuniansky
candidates.keyPriorities: Worker union rights, universal healthcare, and cost-of-living protections for working families.

usHouse.office: U.S. House of Representatives (New Jersey's 11th Congressional District — NJ-11)
usHouse.importance: NJ-11 spans suburban Passaic, Morris, and Essex Counties including Wayne, Parsippany, Montclair, Morristown, and Montville.

candidates.name: Analilia Mejia
candidates.role: U.S. Representative (NJ-11); veteran grassroots organizer and policy advisor.
candidates.keyPriorities: Full federal SALT tax deduction restoration, expanding federal child tax credits, protecting public school funding, and federal flood control grants for the Passaic and Pompton river basins.
candidates.localImpact: Championing federal Army Corps of Engineers funding for Wayne and Passaic County flood basin maintenance.

candidates.name: Joe Hathaway
candidates.role: Randolph Councilman and former Mayor; small business owner and community leader.
candidates.keyPriorities: Federal fiscal restraint, curbing inflation, full SALT relief for suburban homeowners, support for local law enforcement, and business tax cuts.
candidates.localImpact: Advocates for federal infrastructure dollars directed toward North Jersey highway bottlenecks and flood mitigation.

candidates.name: Alan Bond
candidates.keyPriorities: Bipartisan consensus, federal budget balancing, and government accountability.

candidates.name: Vincent Matrisciano
candidates.keyPriorities: Tax relief for working families and reducing federal regulatory overhead.

candidates.keyPriorities: Holding down county property taxes and spending.
